CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 10, 2022
CALL TO ORDER  Al Rios, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at 6:33
  p.m.

INVOCATION  Steve Costley, Acting Director of Parks & Recreation
PLEDGE OF
ALLEGIANCE  Evelyn Garcia, Police Lieutenant

ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Al Rios, Vice Mayor Maria del Pilar Avalos, Council Member
  Maria Davila, and Council Member Gil Hurtado; City Manager Chris
  Jeffers, City Attorney Raul F. Salinas

ABSENT  Council Member Denise Diaz

LATE  City Treasurer Gregory Martinez arrived at the dais at 6:54 p.m.

1
PROCLAMATIONS  The City Council will issue a Proclamation declaring November 10, 2022,
  as Law Enforcement Records and Support Personnel Day.
2
COMMUNITY DEV/
HOUSING  The City Council received and filed a report on the progress of the
  Salvation Army Bell Shelter Pilot Program.
3
MUNICIPAL CODE ADMIN  The City Council conducted a Public Hearing, waived the reading in full
  and introduced Ordinance No. 2022-10-CC entitled - Ordinance amending
  Title 9 (Buildings) of the South Gate Municipal Code by adopting by
  reference the 2022 California Code of Regulations, Title 24 ("2022
  Building Standards Code") and the 2021 International Association of
  Plumbing and Mechanical Officials Codes, by motion of Council Member
  Davila and seconded by Council Member Hurtado.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Davila, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Vice Mayor Avalos, yes; Mayor Rios, yes; Council Member Diaz,
  absent.

  Meredith Elguira, Director of Community Development explains that the
  item before Council is for the adoption of the building code. They are
  bringing it to the Council a little bit earlier they wanted to make sure that
  when the state law goes into effect the city is ready to comply with the
  state law. She continues by explaining that there are significant changes to
  the permit fees, permitting fees, inspections, completion of resident
   SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 10, 2022

3
MUNICIPAL CODE ADMIN
CONT'D  remolding, and board of appeals proceedings. These changes are
  significant enough to were they have to send some of the building and
  planner employees to training so that they will be kept abreast of the latest
  changes in the code. She explains that they have budgeted for that for the
  fiscal year 2022/2023. She explains that these new state mandates are
  effective January 1, 2023 and they propose amendments to the ordinances.
  This concludes her report and is here to answer any questions.

  Mayor Rios clarifies that this is for the building codes.

  Ms. Elguira explains that it is and that this must be renewed every three
  years.

  Vice Mayor Avalos would like to know what the cost of the training is and
  how many employees will be attending.

  Ms. Elguira explains that it ranges from a few hundred dollars, and they
  have three inspectors and one building official. They have already sent
  two inspectors to training, it was all online.

  Vice Mayor Avalos questioned why only two and not all three were sent
  to make sure that it is fair and equitable to all the inspectors because if one
  is out and the other one doesn't have the training it can be difficult.

  Ms. Elguira explains that they are making sure they have someone in the
  field while the other inspector is getting trained.

  Council Member Hurtado questioned the inclusionary percentage is 10%
  percent in terms of the inclusionary housing ordinance.

  Ms. Elguira explains that it is 8%.

  Council Member Hurtado asks that when someone is building a multiple
  unit building what is the percentage that must be inclusionary for low
  income.

  City Manager clarifies that Council Member Hurtado is on item four.

  Mayor Rios asked if anyone in the audience and zoom wished to speak on
  this item. Seeing no one step forward; Mayor Rios closed the audience
  portion.

  Page 2 of 8
   SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 10, 2022
4
MUNICIPAL CODE ADMIN The City Council conducted a Public Hearing and adopted Resolution No.
  2022-67-CC entitled - Resolution of the City Council of the City of South
  Gate, California, establishing the inclusionary housing in lieu fee as
  provided under Chapter 11.29 (Inclusionary Housing), of Division II
  (Zoning Regulations), of Title 11 (Zoning), of the South Gate Municipal,
  by motion of Vice Mayor Avalos and seconded by Council Member
  Davila.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Davila, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Vice Mayor Avalos, yes; Mayor Rios, yes; Council Member Diaz,
  absent.

  Meredith Elguira, Director of Community Development explains that this
  is regarding an ordinance that was adopted back in June. It was explained
  last time that they are going to figure out a new in lieu fee and that is what
  is before Council a proposal for twenty-five dollars per gross square
  footage of residential space. This is in the lower spectrum of what other
  cities are charging, other cities are charging between ten to seventy-one
  dollars for rental unities and fourteen to fifty dollars for townhomes and
  single-family homes. Jim Simon has more information on this item so if
  they have any questions, they can ask him. Going back to the proposed in
  lieu fees is what is happening is that since June they required new
  developments to provide at least 8 percent allocates for affordable housing
  units. They also needed to provide an option for developers to then
  provide other ways to provide affordable housing units if they are unable
  to provide and an in lieu fee is one of those ways a developer can provide
  the city instead of actually providing a unit on the parcel. In order to
  provide them with at least some directions on the fee if they are not going
  to provide the units. Therefore, they came up with the twenty-five dollars
  based on what other cities are charging based on in lieu fees.

  Mayor Rios asks if there is a reason that they are at the lower end.

  Ms. Elguira explains that most of the higher end fees are mostly in cities
  where they will see developers that want or are eager to build housing
  units. Like Santa Monica or LA, they are not really getting a lot of
  developers knocking on the city's door to build housing developments at
  this point. They are talking with a few developers right now but because of
  the construction costs a lot of the developments and no penciling in. She
  provides an example of one developer who was looking at a site on
  Garfield and Imperial but they have tried hard to have housing pencil out
  but they are unable to do that.

  Mayor Rios asked if anyone in the audience and zoom wished to speak on
  this item.
